Rogue Gas Dealers

By: Graham Coetzer | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose and confront the numerous rogue gas dealers putting the lives of the public and their employees at risk in the illicit gas trade in the suburbs of Johannesburg.

Unique Selling Point:
Most members of the public would never realise they are exchanging their home/business gas cylinders for unsafe ones. And while some people will purposely buy illegally filled gas because its cheaper, many other seemingly legit dealers are selling gas they bought on the cheap for the regular retail prices. SO not only is the public being handed a possible ticking time bomb, they are also being ripped off. General retailers, who are buying their gas legally from authorised vendors, are feeling the pinch as they can't compete with rogue gas suppliers.

Summary:
Basically rogue gas dealers fill any cylinders they can get their hands on in the industry. They are not authorised to fill these cylinders. They DO NOT do any safety checks (testing) on the cylinders, yet they fill them up and sell to customers ‘unchecked’ cylinders. Rogues do not do any integrity testing on the cylinders, and why should they, the cylinders do not belong to them, they belong to AFROX, EASIGAS, ORYX, TOTAL, etc etc. It is only these major companies that can do the integrity testing on their cylinders, as they have the proper equipment and trained personnel.

There are reputable dealers buying and selling illegal gas. Majority of the public do not know the dangers involved in purchasing these illegally filled cylinders, although plenty people do know the difference and choose to buy it as they are cheap cheap cheap.

Private Investigator Johan Myburg has been involved in the industry for the past 24 years - and says that since our last insert the illicit industry has kept growing. This is in part due to a larger demand for gas as the SA market is growing constantly - especially with the current electricity crisis. He also says because of poor enforcement from the authorities, organised crime syndicates have now taken control of much of the illegal trade. And because they don't have their own cylinders to use, the major gas companies are now targets, where armed robbers will break into plants, hold up security guards at gunpoint, and literally steal hundreds and in one case more than a thousand cylinders. (We have obtained footage of a break in at a plant called SIMS Gas) (Legal gas retailers, the small shops in malls etc, are afraid to go on camera because of the syndicates, and threats that some of them have received when outing rogues on social media).



Further information:
I have spoken to Kevin Robertson from the Liquified Petroleum Gas Safety Association - they are a NPC who look at safety in the industry. His main concern is for public safety, and says according to their research between 20 and 30% of the gas exchange cylinder market is currently illegally filled and distributed. He has also provided us with dramatic cctv footage of a gas explosion at a private school, caused by a leaking gas cylinder. We can use the footage as long as we don't id the school. Kevin is also able to verify if the cylinders we exchange on hidden cam are illegally filled or not. He can also explain what the public need to be aware of.

This is a consumer story - and one where consumers need to be made aware of what to look out for, because while the authorities are dragging their feet, if consumers stop purchasing the illegal gas, the illicit industry would be brought to its knees.



We are going to go exchange cylinders at three large dealers in JHB who we've been told are operating illegally with a hidden camera. We will then take the cylinders to LPGSA - the Liquified Petroleum Gas Safety Association, a NPC who have a database on all legally filled gas cylinders in SA as well as an expert who can tell if the cylinders were refilled legally and safely.

We will then confront the dealers on camera, hopefully accompanied by the Dept of Labour and the Fire Dept, who we've requested to assist us, who will be either able to issue prohibition notices or shut them down completely.

We have hidden cam footage of illegal gas filling operations, as well as CCTV footage of a gas plant being robbed at night.

Script:


Rogue Gas Dealers
20 November 2019
First Draft

Voice
The local market for Liquefied Petroleum -or LP Gas, is growing steadily - it’s safe, cost effective - and most importantly in modern day South Africa – a reliable source of energy.

Link Devi
It’s the most natural thing in the world - your gas cylinder is empty, so you pop off to the local shop and exchange it. What you may not realise is that you might just have been handed a ticking time bomb.

Voice
And that’s because the lucrative LP Gas market has attracted the attention of people more interested in making a quick buck than the safety of the public. Kevin Robertson is the CEO of the Liquefied Petroleum Gas Safety Association.

Sound Up Kevin
The LP Gas industry is ready to boom - on the negative side unfortunately their’s been an increase in the number of people who are operating illegally, outside of the law.

Voice
We first covered this story in 2014, when we exposed several rogue gas suppliers who were illegally filling and selling LP Gas from unsafe sites like these. Refill cylinders are owned by the consumer, and may be refilled anywhere. But exchange gas cylinders remain the property of the respective gas supplier - you pay a deposit for a cylinder and the brand lends the cylinder to you. These bottles may only be refilled by the companies who own them - it’s legislated in the Occupational Heath and Safety Act.

Sound Up Kevin
It’s an act of parliament, it’s a law. We can’t say it’s a nice to have or naughty naughty don’t, that’s law.

Voice
And there’s a very good reason for that - the major suppliers do cylinder integrity tests, check for overfilling and replace faulty valves if needed. But that’s all wasted time and profit to the rogue suppliers - and a major safety concern.

Sound Up Kevin
Devi: A 9kg bottle, everyone knows that, if that had to go off in a house, what damage could it cause?

Kevin: If it went off in a room like this, it would raise this room. It would be gone.

Voice
From major house fires like this one to injuries in restaurants, there are many examples of when things go wrong. This CCTV footage is from a school. Without any apparent interference, a cylinder explodes, most likely because of a gas leak. And moments later the accumulated gas is seen erupting into an explosive ball of flames. Luckily, the incident happened over a weekend when the school was empty. Robertson says incidents like these are few and far between because LP Gas IS safe to use, if it comes from the legitimate suppliers.

Sound Up Kevin Robertson
Devi: But if we have a run away illegal market, then we start to increase the chances of these kinds of incidents?

Kevin: Very much so.

Voice
Legitimate gas retailers say the rogues are killing their businesses. This man owns a small gas outlet he’s operated successfully for the last four years, but says recently sales have plummeted. We’ll call him Morne’ as he’s asked us to hide his identity for fear of victimisation.

Sound Up “Morne’”
Devi: If you look at business then compared to now, what are the big differences for you?

Morne’: A lot of rogue dealers have been flooding the market recently, in fact this is the first year that we actually took a drop in sales, and I can account a lot of it to be competition from rogues.

Link Devi
Rogue dealers have been getting away with this for years, but it’s gotten worse. Well organised syndicates have smelt the opportunity. Armed and dangerous, they are infiltrating, and gaining ground.

Voice
This man is a private investigator who’s helping authorities identify and prosecute the syndicates. Because of the nature of his work he’s chosen to hide his identity, so we’ll call him Rocky.

Sound Up “Rocky”
Devi: You’re talking about syndicates now, and that takes this story to a whole new level.

Rocky: In the past two years, there has been such a demand for empty cylinders, that I think there was close to 25 armed robberies in the industry. At night, where robbers came, armed to the teeth, with trucks, and they held up the guards, and they steal 500, 600, 700, 1500 cylinders from the company.

Voice
This footage shows one such incident caught on CCTV cameras. A group of men are seen entering a Johannesburg based distributor, and filling a truck they’ve parked inside the premises with their loot. Once the truck is loaded, they disappear off into the night.

Sound Up Rocky
I’ve got a truck, I’ve got empty cylinders, you take it to one of these guys who’s got a bulk tank, he will fill the cylinder for you, and you’re in business.

Voice
Kevin Robertson says this is one story where the public could make all the difference - by refusing to buy illegally filled gas. And spotting it is easy enough, you just need to check the plastic seal shrinkwrapped around the valve when you receive your cylinder.

Sound Up Devi
The branding on the seal needs to match the branding on the bottle, and more often than not you’ll find that the seal has a serial number.

Voice
Fake seals like the one on the left look legit, but don’t show company names or serial numbers. There is no brand called LP Gas, it’s simply the type of gas being sold. If the seal does not have a company brand name on, that cylinder has been illegally refilled. The fake seals have spurred a neat little sideline business for unscrupulous dealers, who will even sell them from car boots as seen in this hidden-camera footage.

Sound Up Kevin Robertson
The consumer has the ability to say no I don’t want that cylinder, I’m bringing you a legit cylinder, I want one that’s been legitimately filled.

Voice
Unfortunately, many illicit cylinders end up being sold to an unsuspecting public by retailers who should know better, whether they refilled them or not. Acting on a tip-off we visited a couple of shops in Johnnesburg. Our first stop …Fairland Hardware and Gas, where we swopped an empty Afrox cylinder for this one, which had the fake LP Gas seal on, and definitely not refilled by Afrox. Our second stop was at Diesel Drive and Oil, where we received this Oryx gas cylinder - in this case the re-fillers hadn’t even bothered with a coloured seal. Private Investigator Rocky says according to the criminal procedure act you cannot benefit financially from an illegal operation, and is working with police to lay charges against anyone refilling or selling illegal gas.

Sound Up Rocky
If I buy from someone who’s filled it illegally, and I’m only selling it, I’m also guilty and you could be charged criminally.

Sound Up Kevin Roberston
Devi: So Kevin, we purchased these two bottles of gas. Can you take a look for me and tell me if there’s something wrong with it?

Kevin: I don’t need much time. That clear seal there indicates immediately that this is an illegally filled cylinder. I mean it gets more sophisticated when you’re looking at this one, because this one is done in the same colours as the brand of the cylinder. But if you have a close up look all it does it has LP Gas on there, and that is a clear indication that it’s an illegally filled cylinder. Because there, the seal should look like this one. Again the logo on the seal must match the logo on the bottle itself. And that’s what the consumer should be looking for. Not this, if you see this, just absolutely say no I do not want that.

Voice
We returned to Fairland Hardware and Gas and met owner Robert Janbroers who didn’t seem happy to see us.

Sound Up Robert
Devi: Hello

Robert: How are you?

Devi: Fine and you.

Robert: Fine thank you.

Devi: Devi Carte Blanche. Come on, shake my hand, it’s not going to be that bad. But you know you’ve got a problem.

Robert: I’ve got a problem?

Devi: Ja, you’ve got a big problem. So we bought gas from you guys, we’ve got the undercover footage, and the gas has been illegally refilled. And we know that for an absolute fact.

Robert: If I have transgressed the law I apologise, I deeply apologise, and I will look into sorting it out.

Devi: So let me show you what I mean, can I show you what I mean in terms of your bottle. You know what I’m going to show you anyway. So I’ve got the exact same, we purchased this from you, I’ve got it here, sealed. This….

Robert: Doesn’t have a number on it.

Devi: Ja, doesn’t have a number on it. You know, it’s not like you don’t know. So you knowingly did the wrong thing, knowingly.

Robert: Did I not just apologise to you inside?

Devi: So who have you been buying this gas from?

Robert: From the same person I’ve bought…

Devi: Who?

Robert: I’m not going to…

Devi: Who? Why don’t you want to out him?

Robert: Im not going to tell you that.

Devi: Yup. Alright.

Robert: Alright, thank you.

Voice
And then it was back to Diesel Drive and Oil, where we met the manager Ian Haldane.

Sound Up Ian Haldane

Devi: see all of them have clear seals.

Ian: Ja.

Devi: So that’s against the law.

Ian: Ja, it’s, ja.

Devi: So whoever is refilling these gas bottles, is refilling illegally.

Ian: yes, ok.

Devi: You know that?

Ian: Yes. And I’m buying it from somebody, and I’m selling it on.

Devi: And you think that thats ok?

Ian: Well I haven’t had a problem yet.

Devi: You waiting for a problem?

Ian: No, I’m not waiting for a problem.

Voice
Haldane said he needed to phone his boss.

Sound Up Ian Haldane
Devi: Whats his name?

Ian: Kobus.

Devi: Surname?

Ian: van der Watt. Kobus, how are you boet? Listen, Carte Blanche is here…

Voice
But van der Watt did not provide any explanations.

Sound Up Ian
Ian: Kobus says I mustn’t answer anymore questions, sorry.

Devi: Can you give me Kobus’ number?

Ian: No unfortunately not.

Devi: Why not?

Ian: Because I don’t give his number to anybody.

Devi: Ja, but this is important now.

Ian: Ma’am, I’m sorry I can’t talk to you any longer.

Voice
As we enter the festive season, it will be up to consumers to decide on who they buy their gas from. But organisations like the LPGSA say when it comes to the gas industry, small decisions could make a huge impact.

Sound Up Kevin Robertson
Kevin: You know we complain that the economy is bad, that sort of thing, but we’re allowing people to come into an industry and destroy the industry, and work against everything that we should be doing.

Devi: And put our lives on the line

Kevin: Absolutely, absolutely.










Promo 1
Voice
The illicit LP Gas trade in South Africa is booming, fuelled by dangerous syndicates with little regard for the public, who are duped into paying for potentially dangerous cylinders.

Promo 2
Voice
Buying an illegally refilled gas cylinder for your home could have deadly consequences - we investigate the rogue gas dealers flooding our market with their illicit goods.

Promo 3
Voice
They’ve been likened to ticking time bombs - illegally refilled gas cylinders are being sold in our suburbs by dangerous syndicates out to dupe an unsuspecting public.

Voice Unfortunately, many illicit cylinders end up being sold to an unsuspecting public by retailers who should know better, whether they refilled them or not. Acting on a tip-off we visited a couple of shops in Johnnesburg. Our first stop …Fairland Hardware and Gas, where we swopped an empty Afrox cylinder for this one, which had the fake LP Gas seal on, and definitely not refilled by Afrox. Our second stop was at Diesel Drive and Oil, where we received this Oryx gas cylinder - in this case the re-fillers hadn’t even bothered with a coloured seal. Private Investigator Rocky says according to the criminal procedure act you cannot benefit financially from an illegal operation, and is working with police to lay charges against anyone refilling or selling illegal gas. Sound Up Rocky If I buy from someone who’s filled it illegally, and I’m only selling it, I’m also guilty and you could be charged criminally. Sound Up Kevin Roberston Devi: So Kevin, we purchased these two bottles of gas. Can you take a look for me and tell me if there’s something wrong with it? Kevin: I don’t need much time. That clear seal there indicates immediately that this is an illegally filled cylinder. I mean it gets more sophisticated when you’re looking at this one, because this one is done in the same colours as the brand of the cylinder. But if you have a close up look all it does it has LP Gas on there, and that is a clear indication that it’s an illegally filled cylinder. Because there, the seal should look like this one. Again the logo on the seal must match the logo on the bottle itself. And that’s what the consumer should be looking for. Not this, if you see this, just absolutely say no I do not want that. Voice We returned to Fairland Hardware and Gas and met owner Robert Janbroers who didn’t seem happy to see us. Sound Up Robert Devi: Hello Robert: How are you? Devi: Fine and you. Robert: Fine thank you. Devi: Devi Carte Blanche. Come on, shake my hand, it’s not going to be that bad. But you know you’ve got a problem. Robert: I’ve got a problem? Devi: Ja, you’ve got a big problem. So we bought gas from you guys, we’ve got the undercover footage, and the gas has been illegally refilled. And we know that for an absolute fact. Robert: If I have transgressed the law I apologise, I deeply apologise, and I will look into sorting it out. Devi: So let me show you what I mean, can I show you what I mean in terms of your bottle. You know what I’m going to show you anyway. So I’ve got the exact same, we purchased this from you, I’ve got it here, sealed. This…. Robert: Doesn’t have a number on it. Devi: Ja, doesn’t have a number on it. You know, it’s not like you don’t know. So you knowingly did the wrong thing, knowingly. Robert: Did I not just apologise to you inside? Devi: So who have you been buying this gas from? Robert: From the same person I’ve bought… Devi: Who? Robert: I’m not going to… Devi: Who? Why don’t you want to out him? Robert: Im not going to tell you that. Devi: Yup. Alright. Robert: Alright, thank you. Voice And then it was back to Diesel Drive and Oil, where we met the manager Ian Haldane. Sound Up Ian Haldane Devi: see all of them have clear seals. Ian: Ja. Devi: So that’s against the law. Ian: Ja, it’s, ja. Devi: So whoever is refilling these gas bottles, is refilling illegally. Ian: yes, ok. Devi: You know that? Ian: Yes. And I’m buying it from somebody, and I’m selling it on. Devi: And you think that thats ok? Ian: Well I haven’t had a problem yet. Devi: You waiting for a problem? Ian: No, I’m not waiting for a problem. Voice Haldane said he needed to phone his boss. Sound Up Ian Haldane Devi: Whats his name? Ian: Kobus. Devi: Surname? Ian: van der Watt. Kobus, how are you boet? Listen, Carte Blanche is here… Voice But van der Watt did not provide any explanations. Sound Up Ian Ian: Kobus says I mustn’t answer anymore questions, sorry. Devi: Can you give me Kobus’ number? Ian: No unfortunately not. Devi: Why not? Ian: Because I don’t give his number to anybody. Devi: Ja, but this is important now. Ian: Ma’am, I’m sorry I can’t talk to you any longer. Voice As we enter the festive season, it will be up to consumers to decide on who they buy their gas from. But organisations like the LPGSA say when it comes to the gas industry, small decisions could make a huge impact. Sound Up Kevin Robertson Kevin: You know we complain that the economy is bad, that sort of thing, but we’re allowing people to come into an industry and destroy the industry, and work against everything that we should be doing. Devi: And put our lives on the line Kevin: Absolutely, absolutely. Promo 1 Voice The illicit LP Gas trade in South Africa is booming, fuelled by dangerous syndicates with little regard for the public, who are duped into paying for potentially dangerous cylinders. Promo 2 Voice Buying an illegally refilled gas cylinder for your home could have deadly consequences - we investigate the rogue gas dealers flooding our market with their illicit goods. Promo 3 Voice They’ve been likened to ticking time bombs - illegally refilled gas cylinders are being sold in our suburbs by dangerous syndicates out to dupe an unsuspecting public.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We expose and confront the numerous rogue gas dealers putting the lives of the public and their employees at risk in the illicit gas trade in the suburbs of Johannesburg.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Most members of the public would never realise they are exchanging their home/business gas cylinders for unsafe ones. And while some people will purposely buy illegally filled gas because its cheaper, many other seemingly legit dealers are selling gas they bought on the cheap for the regular retail prices. SO not only is the public being handed a possible ticking time bomb, they are also being ripped off. General retailers, who are buying their gas legally from authorised vendors, are feeling the pinch as they can't compete with rogue gas suppliers.
metadata.Summary: Basically rogue gas dealers fill any cylinders they can get their hands on in the industry. They are not authorised to fill these cylinders. They DO NOT do any safety checks (testing) on the cylinders, yet they fill them up and sell to customers ‘unchecked’ cylinders. Rogues do not do any integrity testing on the cylinders, and why should they, the cylinders do not belong to them, they belong to AFROX, EASIGAS, ORYX, TOTAL, etc etc. It is only these major companies that can do the integrity testing on their cylinders, as they have the proper equipment and trained personnel. There are reputable dealers buying and selling illegal gas. Majority of the public do not know the dangers involved in purchasing these illegally filled cylinders, although plenty people do know the difference and choose to buy it as they are cheap cheap cheap. Private Investigator Johan Myburg has been involved in the industry for the past 24 years - and says that since our last insert the illicit industry has kept growing. This is in part due to a larger demand for gas as the SA market is growing constantly - especially with the current electricity crisis. He also says because of poor enforcement from the authorities, organised crime syndicates have now taken control of much of the illegal trade. And because they don't have their own cylinders to use, the major gas companies are now targets, where armed robbers will break into plants, hold up security guards at gunpoint, and literally steal hundreds and in one case more than a thousand cylinders. (We have obtained footage of a break in at a plant called SIMS Gas) (Legal gas retailers, the small shops in malls etc, are afraid to go on camera because of the syndicates, and threats that some of them have received when outing rogues on social media).
metadata.Further information: I have spoken to Kevin Robertson from the Liquified Petroleum Gas Safety Association - they are a NPC who look at safety in the industry. His main concern is for public safety, and says according to their research between 20 and 30% of the gas exchange cylinder market is currently illegally filled and distributed. He has also provided us with dramatic cctv footage of a gas explosion at a private school, caused by a leaking gas cylinder. We can use the footage as long as we don't id the school. Kevin is also able to verify if the cylinders we exchange on hidden cam are illegally filled or not. He can also explain what the public need to be aware of. This is a consumer story - and one where consumers need to be made aware of what to look out for, because while the authorities are dragging their feet, if consumers stop purchasing the illegal gas, the illicit industry would be brought to its knees. We are going to go exchange cylinders at three large dealers in JHB who we've been told are operating illegally with a hidden camera. We will then take the cylinders to LPGSA - the Liquified Petroleum Gas Safety Association, a NPC who have a database on all legally filled gas cylinders in SA as well as an expert who can tell if the cylinders were refilled legally and safely. We will then confront the dealers on camera, hopefully accompanied by the Dept of Labour and the Fire Dept, who we've requested to assist us, who will be either able to issue prohibition notices or shut them down completely. We have hidden cam footage of illegal gas filling operations, as well as CCTV footage of a gas plant being robbed at night.
